title: Cold Email v3 Framework
summary: Active cold email framework built from Instantly benchmarks and Belkins 5.5M email study.
content:
Cold Email v3 Framework -- ACTIVE

Built by Alex. Approved by Patrik. Mar 13, 2026. Based on: Instantly 2026 Benchmark Report (billions of emails), Alex Berman framework, Belkins 5.5M email study, Patrik's voice.

Core Principle

The offer is everything. No subject line, no formatting, no follow-up fixes a weak offer. Our old emails had no offer. "Talk shop" is not an offer. Contractors want more jobs, better jobs, and clients who trust them before they show up. Speak to that.

What Changed from v1/v2

Old New Why (Data)
150-200 words 50-80 words 50-125 words get 2.4x higher reply rate (Instantly, 3M emails)
No follow-up 3-touch sequence, Day 0/3/10 Follow-up #1 lifts replies 65.8%. 93% of replies by day 10.
"Talk shop" / no real offer Outcome they care about + "or not really?" Offer is the #1 driver of replies (Instantly framework)
"Really impressed by [Company] work" subject "Hi {first name}" 45.36% open rate, highest performing subject (Belkins, 5.5M emails)
Compliments + case study pitch One proof point baked in naturally Berman: Compliment, Case Study, CTA. But the case study is one phrase, not a paragraph.
Ask for a call Ask for a reply Binary yes/no questions double reply rates vs open-ended asks
"AI-backed content system" Never say AI Contractors buy results, not systems
Signature block Just "Patrik" + default Gmail signature Formal signatures signal mass email
One email, hope for the best 3-email sequence with angles Single emails rarely work. Persistence matters more than volume.

The 3-Email Sequence

EMAIL 1: The Opener

Job: Get a reply. Nothing else.

Subject: "Hi {first name}" (45.36% open rate, #1 performing)

Structure:

{First name},

I work with [a/an] {their trade} contractor in Phoenix on their
video and social media. {One sentence about the outcome --
jobs, trust, inbound calls, not competing on price.}

Is that something {Company}'s thought about or not really?

Have a great weekend.

Patrik

{DEFAULT GMAIL SIGNATURE}

Rules:

  • Under 80 words
  • One proof point baked in ("I work with a contractor" IS the case study)
  • The outcome sentence speaks to what THEY want (jobs, bids, trust) not what WE do (content, production, strategy)
  • CTA is always "or not really?" -- gives them a genuine out, feels like a real person
  • Default Gmail signature included
  • Proper spacing between paragraphs and before sign-off
  • Write it like you just found their site and hit "contact us." Don't over-edit. (Instantly framework)

Never:

  • No company name drop (AOM, Ambition)
  • No links
  • No "impressed," "solid," or flattery
  • No AI mention
  • No service menus
  • No asking for calls
  • No "nah" or "or nah"
  • No "have a good one" (Patrik: "that's asshole")

EMAIL 2: The Value Drop (Day 3, reply to same thread)

Job: Add one new angle. Still not selling.

Subject: (auto: "Re: Hi {first name}")

{First name},

No worries if not. Just figured I'd mention -- we shot one day
with our client and turned it into 30+ posts. They said it was
the first time they got inbound calls from social.

Either way, have a good week.

Patrik

Rules:

  • Reply to same thread (not a new email)
  • One new proof point, one result
  • No pitch, no CTA asking for anything
  • This email works because it adds value without asking

EMAIL 3: The Breakup (Day 10, reply to same thread)

Job: Last touch. Soft close.

Subject: (auto: "Re: Re: Hi {first name}")

{First name},

Last one from me. If {Company} ever wants to explore the
video/social thing, I'm around.

Patrik

Rules:

  • Two sentences max
  • "I'm around" is the CTA
  • No guilt, no "just checking in," no pressure
  • This email often gets the most replies because 3 genuine messages build familiarity

Partnership Email Template

Same principles. Short, honest, "or not really?"

Hey {first name},

I do video and social media for contractors in Phoenix.
{How you found them -- honest.}

Ever open to referral relationships or not really?

Have a great weekend.

Patrik

{DEFAULT GMAIL SIGNATURE}

Critical: Never send to info@, office@, or contact forms. Find the actual person's name and direct email. If you can't find it, skip them.

Metrics & Benchmarks (2026 data)

Metric Bad Average Good Great
Open rate Below 30% 40-50% 50-60% 65%+
Reply rate Below 2% 3-5% 5-10% 10%+
Positive reply rate Below 1% 2-3% 3-5% 5%+

Below 2% reply rate for 3 weeks straight = pivot the message entirely.

Source: Instantly 2026 Benchmark Report, Belkins 2025 study (5.5M emails)

Infrastructure (approved, needs purchase)

What Why Cost
3-5 secondary domains Protect aom-inhouse.com, spread volume ~$10-15/domain/year
Instantly or Smartlead Sending, warm-up, tracking, sequences ~$30-40/month
SPF/DKIM/DMARC on each domain Required by Gmail/Yahoo 2026 Free (DNS config)
Email verification (MillionVerifier) Keep bounces under 2% ~$20/month
4-6 week warm-up period New domains need ramp before volume Time only

Current: 1 domain, ~15 sends/day safe Target: 100/domain/day x 3-5 domains = 300-500/day

Reply Playbook (what happens when they respond)

  1. Reply within 2 hours. Speed > perfection.
  2. Ask ONE qualifying question: "How are you getting most of your jobs right now?"
  3. If they engage, offer a 10-minute call (not 30, not 15)
  4. On the call: learn their situation, show ambitionac.com as proof, propose the retainer
  5. Never send pricing over email. Pricing is a conversation.

What We DON'T Say (Hard Rules)

  • No "AI-backed" or "AI-powered" anything
  • No free work offers (killed Mar 12)
  • No service menus or pricing in cold email
  • No links in email 1 or 3
  • No asks for calls until they reply first
  • No "impressed" or "solid" (overused, sounds fake at scale)
  • No naming other clients (unless completely different trade)
  • No "nah"
  • No "have a good one"
  • No "collaboration" or "collab" (implies mutual project, misleading for cold intro)
  • No "quick question" (overused subject line)

Status

  • v3 framework: ACTIVE. Source of truth for all outreach.
  • v1 (Patrik original): Retired. Good voice, weak structure.
  • v2 (zero-risk offer): DEAD per council ruling Mar 12.
  • 78-draft review packet: KILLED. Old voice. Do not send.
  • Monday batch (5 emails): APPROVED. Schedule Mon Mar 16, 11am AZ.
